name: read
description: Read a file (relative to the workspace, or absolute). Text comes back numbered `cat -n` style (line number, tab, text): up to 2000 lines from `offset` (1-based, default 1), or `limit` lines; a result that stops early says how to continue. Lines over 2000 characters are cut. Images (png, jpg, gif, webp) come back as images, PDFs as text per page (`pages`, e.g. "1-5"; at most 20 per call, required above 10 pages), Jupyter notebooks as cells with their outputs (for a notebook, `offset` is a 0-based cell index and `limit` a number of cells). Read a file before you edit or overwrite it, and never copy the line-number prefix into an edit.

limit.description: Number of lines (for a notebook, cells) to return.

offset.description: 1-based line to start from (for a notebook, a 0-based cell index).

path.description: File path, relative to the workspace or absolute.

name: write
description: Create a file, or replace an existing one entirely with `content`; parent directories are created. Overwriting an existing file needs a `read` of it first in this session; it keeps its byte-order mark and CRLF line endings. Prefer `edit` for a change to part of a file.

name: edit
description: Replace `old_string` with `new_string` in one file. `old_string` must occur exactly once (copy it from `read` without the line-number prefix, with enough surrounding lines to be unique), or set `replace_all` to change every occurrence. A match that differs only in line endings or by one uniform indentation still applies when it is unique, and the result says so. `read` the file first in this session. To create a file use `write`.

name: multi_edit
description: Several `edit`s at once, in one or more files, applied all together or not at all. Edits run in order, each seeing the result of the ones before it. `path` is the default file; an edit may name its own. An empty `old_string` creates a file that does not exist. `read` each existing file first.

path.description: The file the edits apply to unless an edit names its own.

name: edit_lines
description: Edit lines by anchor. `read` shows each line as `N:hhh|text`; name a line by its anchor `N:hhh` (and the last line of a range by `end`). `op`: replace (default), insert_after, insert_before or delete. An anchor whose line changed since you read it is refused with fresh anchors. `anchor` "0" with insert_after writes at the top of the file.

end.description: Anchor of the last line of the range (default: `anchor`).

name: notebook_edit
description: Edit one cell of a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). `cell` is the cell's id or 0-based index as `read` shows it. `mode`: replace (default) the cell's source, insert a new cell after `cell` (at the top without one), or delete it. `cell_type` sets the new cell's type and changes it on replace. Replacing a code cell clears its outputs. `read` the notebook first.
